subject: Private deployment: KMS/HSM integration, operator separation & unseal flow
messages:
From: SecureBank Security <secops@securebank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: HSMCo Integrations <integration@hsmco.com>, AcmeCloud PM <pm@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: KMS integration & operator model for private deploy

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. As we prepare for the on-prem pilot of Redwood Private in our staging DC, the security team has a few architecture questions we need written confirmation on before procurement: 

1) Unseal / auto-unseal model: do you require Vault auto-unseal against a cloud KMS, or can Redwood support a KMIP-backed HSM cluster in our DMZ for auto-unseal?

2) BYOK / key import: we plan to BYOK and retain root key material in our HSM (HSMCo appliance). What import formats do you accept (PKCS #12 / PKCS#11 wrapped blobs / KMIP)?

3) Operator privileges: we need explicit controls to avoid operators being able to extract key material (approval flows, split roles, HSM operator vs infra operator separation).

4) Rotation and emergency rotate: proposed rotation cadence, and a one-hour emergency rotate playbook for compromised node scenarios.

5) Audit and retention: what audit logs does Redwood forward, and can logs be sent to our SIEM (SecureBank Splunk) without leaking key identifiers?

I've attached a short questionnaire and a rough rack diagram. Can you respond with a short design note and a proposed follow-up (call + on-site HSM check)?

Thanks,
Rachel Meyer
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Security
SecureBank

Attachment: rack-diagram-dc-1.pdf (PDF)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: SecureBank Security <secops@securebank.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, sofi a_ivanova@redwood.ai, HSMCo Integrations <integration@hsmco.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: KMS integration & operator model for private deploy

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear list. Summary answer up front: Redwood Private can integrate with KMIP-backed HSMs (on-prem) and supports both BYOK imports (KMIP/PKCS#11 wrapped blobs) and cloud KMS auto-unseal where customers prefer managed keys. We recommend a hybrid design for SecureBank: primary key custodianship in your HSM, Redwood-managed ephemeral unseal keys and a split-operator model.

I've written a short design note below and attached a diagram and an emergency rotate playbook. Happy to jump on a call — propose Tue 19 Jan 15:00 ET.

Design highlights (high level):
- Key custody: customer retains root key (BYOK) in on-prem HSM (KMIP preferred). Redwood stores sealed key blobs only; unsealing requires a KMIP operation that is gated by customer HSM policies.
- Auto-unseal: support KMIP Unwrap/Sign flow. For environments that cannot allow network calls to HSM for unseal, we offer a vault server with TPM-based node attestation + sealed blob distribution for offline unseal.
- Operator separation: split roles into HSM Operators (customer-side) and Redwood infra operators. Redwood operators can perform node lifecycle and restart but cannot request raw unwrapped key material. HSM actions (unwrap/export) require multi-person approval configured in HSMCo and mirrored by Redwood's canary-safe handshake.
- Rotation & emergency: recommend 90-day rotation for data-encryption keys; root wrapping keys (customer HSM root) on a 1y cadence unless policy dictates otherwise. Emergency rotate playbook attached.
- Auditing: Redwood forwards audit events (unseal attempts, key-access API calls, node_id, request_id) to customer SIEM over TLS; we redact raw key material and only include key IDs and HSM operation metadata.

See the more technical reply from Marcus below for implementation details (KMIP/PKCS#11, PKCS#7 wrapped blobs, KMIP policy enforcement).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-kms-arch-diagram.png (PNG), playbook-rotate-emergency.pdf (PDF)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: SecureBank Security <secops@securebank.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Rachel / team — technical appendix below to the high-level note. I'll call out concrete protocols and operator constraints so your security architecture team can review.

--- technical appendix ---
1) Accepted import/unwrap formats
   - KMIP 1.3+ (preferred): Redwood acts as a KMIP client to your HSM for Unwrap/Decrypt/Sign operations. Import via KMIP SymmetricKeyImport or wrapped PKCS#7 is supported.
   - PKCS#11: Redwood supports PKCS#11 calls via an HSM proxy when customers expose a PKCS#11 endpoint. We recommend KMIP for richer policy metadata.

2) Auto-unseal options
   - Online KMIP unseal: Vault auto-unseal against customer HSM. During bootstrap, Redwood requests an Unwrap operation using the customer key; HSM policy restricts the originating Redwood client certificate and enforces multi-user approval where required.
   - TPM-assisted sealed blobs: For air-gapped DCs, Redwood will provision sealed blobs encrypted to node TPM EK/AK. On node boot, TPM attestation + Redwood agent unlocks the runtime key material. Those sealed blobs are stored in a customer-controlled artifact store (S3/GCS/On-prem object) and require operator authorization to update.

3) Operator separation and least privilege
   - HSM operator (customer): holds HSM admin roles, approves unwrap/import operations.
   - Redwood infra operator: can restart services, update config, view usage metrics, cannot trigger Unwrap/Export.
   - Break-glass: emergency key unseal requires two customer HSM operators + one Redwood on-call acknowledgement; all actions open a timebound window and emit immediate audit stream to customer SIEM.

4) Cryptographic hygiene and rotation
   - Root KEK (in customer HSM): rotate annually and rotate wrapped data keys on a 90-day schedule.
   - Maintain key version pointers in Redwood's config; rotation is atomic using a dual-write epoch and canary traffic before full cutover.

5) Audit & telemetry
   - Events emitted: unseal_attempt, kmip_op_type, node_id, cert_thumbprint, request_id, result_status. No raw key material or key plaintext in logs.
   - Transport: syslog/HTTP(S) to customer SIEM with mTLS and cert pinning.

6) Network segmentation recommendations
   - HSM endpoints must be in a dedicated management VLAN/Subnet; KMIP/TLS allowed only from Redwood's management jump-hosts. No direct worker node KMIP access in default setup; worker nodes only receive sealed blobs.

If helpful, we can provide a short validation checklist for your HSM team to run during on-site testing.

- Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Forwarding the proposed operator controls and a short policy snippet you can import into your HSMCo appliance. Note this is intentionally conservative — we can relax multi-person approval for lower-sensitivity test environments.

----- Forwarded message -----
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-19T14:00:00Z
Subject: Operator separation policy snippet
To: SecureBank Security <secops@securebank.com>

Policy snippet (pseudo-KMIP role mapping):
- ROLE_HSM_OP: can import/wrap/unwrap only when 2-of-3 approvers sign the operation token.
- ROLE_REDH_OP: can request unseal but the HSM will respond with "pending" until HSM_OPs approve.
- ROLE_AUDITOR: read-only access to operation logs; logs are forwarded to SecureBank SIEM in real time.

Playbook: emergency rotate
1) Initiate rotate request in Redwood Console (creates rotate request, displays affected nodes).
2) HSMCo appliance: approve 2-of-3 -> Unwrap new wrapping key -> return wrapped blob.
3) Redwood: dual-write new key pointer, route 5% canary traffic for 15 minutes, if ok -> full cutover.
4) Emit audit: rotate_event, affected_nodes, operator_ids, request_id.

Attachment: playbook-rotate-emergency.pdf

Regards,
Vivek
VP, Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
